rdfs:label: 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole

rdfs:label: cobamamide

rdfs:label: nicotinate

rdfs:label: hydrogenphosphate

rdfs:label: nicotinate D-ribonucleotide(2-)
IAO:0000115: Dianion of nicotinic acid <small>D</small>-ribonucleotide arising from deprotonation of carboxylic acid and phosphate functions.

rdfs:label: alpha-ribazole 5'-phosphate(2-)
IAO:0000115: Dianion of α-ribazole 5'-phosphate arising from deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups; major species at pH 7.3.

rdfs:label: guanosine 5'-monophosphate(2-)
IAO:0000115: A nucleoside 5'-monophosphate(2−) that results from the removal of two protons from the phosphate group of GMP.

rdfs:label: adenosylcobinamide guanosyl diphosphate(1-)
IAO:0000115: An organophosphate oxoanion that is the anion of adenosylcobinamide guanosyl diphosphate with overall charge −1, arising from deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups; major species at pH 7.3.

rdfs:label: adenosylcobalamin 5'-phosphate(2-)
IAO:0000115: The conjugate base of adenosylcobalamin 5'-phosphate, formed by loss of two protons from the 5'-phosphate group.

comment:
<comment datatype="string">This pathway describes the late steps in the biosynthesis of adenosylcobalamin starting with <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ADENOSYLCOBINAMIDE-GDP">adenosylcobinamide-GDP</a> - the last common intermediate used for the synthesis of cobamides with different lower ligand bases. By definition, the lower ligand base of cobalamin-type B12 vitamins is <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=DIMETHYLBENZIMIDAZOLE">5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole</a>.
<p>
In this pathway <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=DIMETHYLBENZIMIDAZOLE">5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole</a> is tethered to the corrin ring via a structure known as the nucleotide loop, which is composed from <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=R-1-AMINOPROPAN-2-YL-PHOSPHATE">(<i>R</i>)-1-amino-2-propanol <i>O</i>-2-phosphate</a> and <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=DIMETHYLBENZIMIDAZOLE">5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole</a>.
<p>
Until 2007 it was believed that the last reaction in the biosynthesis of <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ADENOSYLCOBALAMIN">adenosylcobalamin</a> was the linking of <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ALPHA-RIBAZOLE">&alpha;-ribazole</a> (a product of <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=DIMETHYLBENZIMIDAZOLE">5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole</a>) to <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ADENOSYLCOBINAMIDE-GDP">adenosylcobinamide-GDP</a>, in a reaction catalyzed by cobalamine synthase. However, it has been shown that at least in <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-90371"><i>Salmonella enterica</i> enterica serovar Typhimurium</a> the true substrate for the enzyme is <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ALPHA-RIBAZOLE-5-P">&alpha;-ribazole 5'-phosphate</a>, and not <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ALPHA-RIBAZOLE">&alpha;-ribazole</a> [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17209023">Zayas07</a>], and that the product of the reaction is actually <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ADENOSYLCOBALAMIN-5-P">adenosylcobalamin 5'-phosphate</a>. Thus, there is one more reaction in the pathway, the dephosphorylation of <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ADENOSYLCOBALAMIN-5-P">adenosylcobalamin 5'-phosphate</a> to <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ADENOSYLCOBALAMIN">adenosylcobalamin</a>, which is catalyzed by <a href="/gene?orgid=META&id=MONOMER-13213">adenosylcobalamin/&alpha;-ribazole phosphatase</a>, the enzyme initially proposed to catalyze the dephosphorylation of <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ALPHA-RIBAZOLE-5-P">&alpha;-ribazole 5'-phosphate</a> [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17209023">Zayas07</a>].
<p>
This model addresses several questions that were associated with the previous model, such as the presence of <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ADENOSYLCOBALAMIN-5-P">adenosylcobalamin 5'-phosphate</a> (which has been documented much earlier in the organism <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-1752"><i>Propionibacterium freudenreichii</i> shermanii</a> [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/4296474">Friedmann68</a>]), the higher affinity of the CobS protein (and its homologs in other organisms) towards <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ALPHA-RIBAZOLE-5-P">&alpha;-ribazole 5'-phosphate</a>, and the inability of <a href="/gene?orgid=META&id=G-10054">cobC</a> mutants to salvage cobyrate under aerobic conditions [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17209023">Zayas07</a>].
<p>
For more information, please see the summaries for the pathways <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=PWY-5507">adenosylcobalamin biosynthesis I (anaerobic)</a> and <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=P381-PWY">adenosylcobalamin biosynthesis II (aerobic)</a>.</comment>

comment: <comment datatype="string">The CobC protein has not been characterised in <i>E. coli</i> K-12 but is predicted to be an adenosylcobalamin 5'-phosphate phosphatase by homology with <i>cobC</i> from <i>Salmonella typhimurium</i>. Early studies in <i>S. typhimurium</i> suggested that CobC was an &alpha;-ribazole phosphatase [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7929373">OToole94</a>] but more recently it was shown that adenosylcobalamin 5'-phosphate was the preferred substrate and that CobC catalyses the last step of adenosylcobalamin (coenzyme B12) biosynthesis [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17209023">Zayas07</a>].</comment>

comment:
<comment datatype="string"><i>E. coli</i> K-12, as well as natural isolates, can synthesize cobalamin only when supplied with the intermediate
cobinamide [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/8770581">Lawrence96</a>].  <i>cobS</i> encodes a cobalamin 5'-phosphate synthase [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17209023">Zayas07</a>] that carries out the penultimate step in adenosylcobalamin synthesis.
<p>
Expression of the <i>cobUST</i> operon is induced by cobinamide [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7592411">Lawrence95</a>].
</comment>

name: Dimethylbenzimidazole + nicotinate β-D-ribonucleotide → Hydrogen Ion + N1-(5-Phospho-a-D-ribosyl)-5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole + Nicotinic acid

texts.value: Catalyzes the synthesis of alpha-ribazole-5'-phosphate from nicotinate mononucleotide (NAMN) and 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole (DMB)
Nucleoside biosynthesis; alpha-ribazole biosynthesis; alpha-ribazole from 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole: step 1/2

Joins adenosylcobinamide-GDP and alpha-ribazole to generate adenosylcobalamin (Ado-cobalamin). Also synthesizes adenosylcobalamin 5'-phosphate from adenosylcobinamide-GDP and alpha-ribazole 5'-phosphate (By similarity)
Cofactor biosynthesis; adenosylcobalamin biosynthesis; adenosylcobalamin from cob(II)yrinate a,c-diamide: step 7/7

Catalyzes the conversion of adenosylcobalamin 5'-phosphate to adenosylcobalamin (vitamin B12); involved in the assembly of the nucleotide loop of cobalamin. Also catalyzes the hydrolysis of the phospho group from alpha-ribazole 5'-phosphate to form alpha-ribazole
Nucleoside biosynthesis; alpha-ribazole biosynthesis; alpha-ribazole from 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole: step 2/2
Belongs to the phosphoglycerate mutase family

evidence.source_assertion: Salmonella CobC-containing extract dephosphorylated the cobalamin phosphate formed by nucleotide-loop assembly; vector-only extract did not. Corrinoids were cyanated before HPLC analysis.
